why: The campaign's registry views (cases.json, inventory.json) are generated by campaign.py, which measures a macOS app and cannot run on Windows. Editing the .in.json inputs here would leave the derived views stale, which is the same 'a registry a person edits cannot also be the witness that the edit was earned' failure the repository's own gates exist against. These rows are therefore a PROPOSAL to be merged and regenerated on macOS, not an edit.
measuredAgainst: MCPRouter.AutomationProbe (app/windows/AutomationProbe), NOT the MCP Router Windows client, which has no drawable window yet (WIN3).
idNote: SURF-018 was tried first and is TAKEN. surfaces.in.json stops at SURF-017 for the glass lanes, so it looked free; inventory.json already holds SURF-018 as an ios-glass surface, because the inventory is generated from more sources than the input file. SURF-029 is the first id free in BOTH.

surfaces.title: Windows automation probe — WinUI 3 UIA plane
surfaces.routeNote: not a product surface. It is the instrument WIN20 built to measure what a WinUI 3 window publishes on the UI Automation plane, so the thirteen Windows surfaces are not built on an unmeasured assumption. When WIN3 lands its shell, the product surfaces get their own ids and this one stays as the channel's own control.

lanes.note: out-of-process UI Automation client, Windows PowerShell 5.1 + System.Windows.Automation, reading a window that is drawn and never foregrounded. Requires window station WinSta0; the lane refuses any other station with exit 3 rather than reading an empty tree as a pass.

requirements.text: A Windows surface publishes a UI Automation tree in which every control is individually addressable by AutomationId, with names matching the on-screen vocabulary, readable out of process without the window being activated or foregrounded.
requirements.providerNote: the provider is the framework's own automation peers; the campaign reads them, it does not implement them.

requirements.text: A Windows control's state — disabled, selected, held and busy — is readable from the automation plane rather than from pixels.
requirements.providerNote: disabled via the IsEnabled property; selected via SelectionPattern and SelectionItemPattern; held via TogglePattern; busy via the localised 'Busy' marker WinUI prepends to an active ProgressRing's name, since it exposes no usable RangeValuePattern state.

cases.note: 20 controls, each resolving to exactly one element, each Name equal to the manifest's on-screen word. The expectation manifest is written by hand from DESIGN.md §11 and REQ-003's destination words, not generated from the XAML it checks.
all four states read off the plane. Selection is asserted on two different providers — a NavigationView and a ListView — because one provider agreeing with itself is one measurement, not two.

the never-foregrounded invariant. Three bracketed GetForegroundWindow samples, none of them the target. Asserted as 'the target never held the foreground', not 'the foreground never changed' — see planning/evidence/M34-oracle-lane.md for what the second phrasing cost.

a CommandBar's SecondaryCommands are not realised while the overflow is closed — absent from the control view AND the raw view. Two conditions would open a rung: the harness opens the overflow, which mutates the surface it is measuring and gives up the never-activated guarantee; or the command is also reachable from a surface realised at rest. The second is the fix. This bears on DESIGN.md §11 rule 9 and belongs to WIN3's construction, not to the harness.
